improvements: The verifiable hash demo is the credibility centerpiece but currently conflates two things: FNV-1a of arbitrary bytes (trivially verifiable) vs. the canonical 0xbf27a3631cdee337 which requires the full cellToDials() pipeline. Ship a 'reproduce the canonical hash' REPL/paste-a-dials demo, or link to a CI log/test output showing all 13 languages emitting identical hashes — otherwise the 13-language claim rests on prose.

Project cards say 'click through to the code' but repo names appear as bare text (quilt, quilt-cell, federated-tinyml-vessel) with no visible full URLs in the content — render absolute github.com/SuperInstance/<repo> links so trust survives copy-paste, archives, and screen readers, and add last-commit dates or star counts per repo as freshness signals.

The lede still makes sweeping claims a skeptic will bounce off ('all byte-exact across 13 languages', 'the whole stack runs on a $5 chip') without inline citations. Anchor each hero claim to a section anchor (e.g. '$5 chip → See F170 hardware spec') and move unverifiable marketing adjectives ('a spreadsheet that thinks', 'vector-memory ocean') below the fold so the first 60 seconds are pure verifiable fact.
